name: Rosalyn S. Yalow
summary: American medical physicist and Nobel laureate who co-developed radioimmunoassay.

name: Solomon Berson
summary: American physician and scientist who partnered with Yalow to develop radioimmunoassay.

name: Hunter College
summary: Tuition-free, all-female college in New York City where Yalow majored in physics.

name: University of Illinois
summary: University that accepted Yalow into their PhD program in nuclear physics.

name: Veterans Administration Hospital
summary: Hospital in the Bronx where Yalow worked and established the radioisotope unit.

name: radioimmunoassay
summary: Analytical method for measuring concentrations of antigens using antibodies and radioisotopes.

name: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1977
summary: Award presented to Rosalyn Yalow for the development of radioimmunoassay.

name: The Journal of Clinical Investigation
summary: Biomedical journal that published Yalow and Berson's key 1960 paper.

name: American Society for Clinical Investigation
summary: Organization whose annual meeting hosted the first public presentation of radioimmunoassay.

name: Karolinska Institute
summary: Institute where Yalow delivered her Nobel Lecture.

name: Swedish Academy
summary: Academy where Yalow accepted her Nobel Prize.

name: King Carl XVI Gustaf
summary: King of Sweden who presented the Nobel Prize to Yalow.

name: the Bronx
summary: Borough of New York City where Yalow was born, educated, and worked.

name: New Jersey
summary: State where Yalow was buried.

name: Atlantic City
summary: City where the 1960 radioimmunoassay presentation occurred and where Berson died.

name: Stockholm
summary: City where Yalow received the Nobel Prize.

name: Aaron Yalow
summary: Husband of Rosalyn Yalow.

name: Ben Yalow
summary: Child of Rosalyn Yalow.

name: Elanna Yalow
summary: Child of Rosalyn Yalow.

name: Jesse Roth
summary: Author of the tribute and former fellow in Yalow's lab.
